record.paper_title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems
record.context_brief: Vanishing Jacobian in W2,q or WBV
record.original_question: Let n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q < n/2. Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f in the Sobolev space W^{2,q} with Jacobian Jf = 0 almost everywhere? The same question is also asked for homeomorphisms whose first-order derivative belongs to the space of bounded variation, that is, for f ∈ WBV.

evidence.quote: Open problem 13. Can the Jacobian of W2,1 (or W BV ) homeomorphism vanish: Let n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q < n/2. Is it possible to construct a Sobolev W2,q homeomorphism with Jf = 0 a.e.? The same problem could be asked also for f ∈ W BV, i.e. for homeomorphism with first order derivative in the space of bounded variation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer and let $q$ be a real number with $1 \leq q < n/2$. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain (e.g. the open unit cube $(0,1)^n$). 

Recall that a map $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W^{2,q}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n)$ if $f$ and all its first- and second-order distributional partial derivatives belong to $L^q(\Omega)$. The Jacobian of $f$ is $J_f(x) = \det Df(x)$, defined almost everywhere via the (a.e. existing) classical derivative.

A map $f$ is said to have first-order derivative of bounded variation, written $f \in W\!BV(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n)$, if $f \in W^{1,1}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and each component of $Df$ belongs to the space $BV(\Omega)$ of functions of bounded variation.

Question (two parts):
(a) Does there exist a homeomorphism $f : \Omega \to f(\Omega) \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f \in W^{2,q}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $J_f(x) = 0$ for almost every $x \in \Omega$?
(b) Does there exist a homeomorphism $f : \Omega \to f(\Omega) \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f \in W\!BV(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $J_f(x) = 0$ for almost every $x \in \Omega$?

Construct such homeomorphisms or prove that none exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an explicit open problem in a 2025 survey on the Ball–Evans approximation problem. While the analogous question for W^{1,p} homeomorphisms has been resolved (Hencl and others constructed Sobolev homeomorphisms with zero Jacobian a.e. for p < n), the W^{2,q} and WBV cases for n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q < n/2 do not appear to be resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a recent survey (2025).

status_evidence.title: Sobolev homeomorphism with zero Jacobian almost everywhere
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of W^{1,p} homeomorphisms with vanishing Jacobian a.e. for p < n.
status_evidence.claim: The W^{1,p} analogue is solved; the W^{2,q} version remains the natural open extension.
